input_candidate_proposals.reason: The landlord's petition alleged that West sublet, assigned, or otherwise parted with possession to Caravan; this is a claimed proposition, not an established transfer.
West expressly denied any subletting, assignment, or parting with possession; the binding preserves the submission as a candidate counter-proposition only.
West claimed that it remained in possession of the premises, which is candidate evidence against a parting-with-possession theory; target acceptance is not imported into the binding.
The landlord claimed that West had gone out of the picture and Caravan alone possessed the premises, a candidate proposition supporting parting with possession.

input_candidate_proposals.reason: The landlord alleged that the asserted transfer occurred without obtaining consent. This supports the no-consent predicate only as an allegation and does not establish a distinct finding about written consent.

target_refs.quote: the Madras-Bangalore Transport Company (West) continued to be in occupation of the premises even after the Caravan Goods Carrier Private Limited came in. They never effaced themselves.
We do not think that there was any sub-letting, assignment or parting with possession of the premises

target_witnesses.reason: The target court expressly found continued occupation by West and expressly rejected subletting, assignment, or parting with possession; this is nonfulfilment of the transfer/possession element, not merely a failure of proof.

The target court did not separately decide the statutory date predicate. The 1968 formation of Caravan and the 1979 petition chronology do not establish the date of a qualifying transfer, especially because the court found no such transfer.

The target court did not expressly adopt a finding that written landlord consent was absent. The frozen input contains only the landlord's allegation, and the target disposed of the section 14(1)(b) ground on the no-transfer determination.
